extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and editors of Renaissance literature / readers of an annotated edition of Castiglione's The Courtier
extracted.subtask_description: Scholarly explanatory notes and editorial commentary for an annotated edition of Baldassare Castiglione's The Courtier, identifying persons, places, textual variants, sources, and translator decisions. Intended to clarify historical, geographical, and textual points for readers and researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translator choice to reproduce original rather than translate
rubrics_metrics.description: The translator may prefer not to render certain Italian passages into English and instead reprint them line for line from a source edition (e.g., the Aldine folio of 1528).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a passage is left untranslated, indicate the source edition from which the original is reproduced and explain the translator's preference. Example on page 213: translator reprinted the Italian lines from the Aldine folio of 1528 rather than offer an English version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly note any suppression or omission by the translator
rubrics_metrics.description: Any instance where the translator suppresses or omits part of the original text should be identified in the notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the exact location and nature of the suppression (e.g., 'The only other instance in which the translator has suppressed any part of the text is in line 10 of page 212, where the Italian word igntida is not rendered').

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and report variant manuscript and edition readings
rubrics_metrics.description: When earlier manuscripts or other editions present variant wordings of a passage, report these variants and, where useful, quote them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the differing readings (verbatim if possible), cite which manuscripts or editions they come from, and explain how the variants affect sense or interpretation. Several notes show this practice (e.g., alternate reading of the passage about the peasant girl's name in two earlier MS versions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference and cite contemporary documentary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: If a story or detail appears elsewhere (letters, chronicles, other authors), identify and cite that source and note any differences in names or details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the external source citation and summarise the variant details (example: Matteo Bandello's letter giving the girl's name as Giulia and naming the Bishop as Ludovico Gonzaga).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify historical persons with dates, relationships, and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concise biographical identification for persons mentioned (birth/death approximate dates, family ties, offices held), to situate them historically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dates where known, relevant family or political connections, and references to further authorities (examples throughout: Ludovico Gonzaga, Felice della Rovere, Henry VIII, Charles V).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide geographical identification and modern equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain place-names, their modern forms, locations, and notable geographic facts relevant to understanding the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give contemporary place names, distances, and distinguishing features (e.g., 'Gazuolo or Gazzuolo is now the name of an Italian commune, less than 5,000 inhabitants, eleven miles west of Mantua'; Volturno flows through Capua; Oglio river details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite and identify classical and literary source references
rubrics_metrics.description: When the text alludes to or draws upon classical authors or works (Ovid, Plutarch, Ars Amandi, The Republic, etc.), identify the source and, where possible, the book/lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the classical work and passage (e.g., 'reference here is to Ovid's Ars Amandi' or 'the reference is to Book V of The Republic'), and note the influence or derivation of the passage in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag and discuss internal chronological or textual inconsistencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out and comment on apparent inconsistencies within the primary text (tense, anachronism, conflicting identifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the inconsistency and, if feasible, suggest explanations or indicate which manuscript reading may resolve it (example: Castiglione's use of present tense inconsistent with Canossa's later title; note 431 cites this).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concise bibliographic or authority references for asserted facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Support factual assertions in notes (dates, identifications, architectural attributions) with citations to secondary literature or archival authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting particulars (e.g., building dates, costs, authorship), cite articles, books, or archival sources used (example: citation of Rossi in Giornale Storico della Letteratura Italiana; Luzio and Renier's Mantova e Urbino).
